channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 75: Clay Every Which Way
item.description: The 75th issue of the UK independent art zine Haus-a-rest, edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers, takes clay as its subject — but explicitly not clay as pottery. The editors want work that goes beyond the pot, beyond tradition and beyond expectation: clay as unfired material, slip, earth pigment, digital simulation, or as a metaphor for transformation, identity, labour, geology, archaeology, ritual, play, memory and the body. Photography is named among the accepted media alongside sculpture, installation, painting, drawing, printmaking, textiles incorporating clay, mixed media, land art, performance documentation, video (YouTube links only) and digital works, and the call runs in parallel for writers submitting poetry, essays, short fiction, creative non-fiction and experimental texts. Conceptual responses are welcomed as warmly as material ones — the editors ask what it means to shape something with your hands, how clay remembers touch, and whether a material can carry history, culture or politics. Submit up to three artworks as JPEGs, or up to 1,000 words of writing, or a combination, together with titles, a statement of no more than 200 words explaining how the work fits the theme, and a biography of up to 150 words. An Instagram handle is required: selected contributors are asked to collaborate on sharing the posts. There is no submission fee, the call is open internationally to artists and writers at every career stage, and selected work is published in the online zine and gallery and promoted across the zine's social channels. Entry closes 3 September 2026 through CuratorSpace. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Forms and Fragments · Atlantic Gallery
item.description: The first annual online juried competition from Atlantic Gallery, the artist-run cooperative that has operated in Chelsea since 1974. Forms and Fragments asks artists to explore the relationship between what is transformed, remembered, assembled or broken, and the shapes those experiences become — the beauty of what remains, what is reconstructed and what emerges. Work may investigate memory, identity, landscape, culture, architecture, the body or abstraction through literal or symbolic fragments and evolving forms, considering how the parts relate to the whole, and the gallery invites personal, political, material and conceptual readings alike. The juror is Patricia Miranda, an artist, curator and educator who founded The Crit Lab and MAPSpace and the Lace Archive, and who has held residencies at the Textile Art Center, Vermont Studio Center, I-Park and Weir Farm. Photography is listed among the accepted media, alongside oils, acrylics, watercolours, pastels, drawings, traditional printmaking, original digital art, fibre art, mixed media and sculpture in any medium; digital or giclée reproductions of original artwork and AI-generated work are excluded. Entry is open to all artists 18 and over, at $30 for up to three works plus $10 for up to five more submitted at the same time, with no piece larger than 32 inches in any direction. Selected work is shown in an online exhibition running 1 October to 12 November 2026 and reproduced in an online digital catalogue, and every accepted piece is featured on the gallery's social channels. The award is the significant part: prize winners are selected for inclusion in Atlantic Gallery's physical group show in its Chelsea space, 1–19 December 2026, with work delivered in person or by proxy. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 images), $10 for 5 more. Prize: Group exhibition in Chelsea, NYC.

item.title: Jazz Got Loose at The Gallery at the Attucks · Norfolk Arts
item.description: Norfolk Arts, the City of Norfolk's public arts agency, is filling the next six-month rotation at The Gallery at the Attucks, inside the historic Attucks Theatre in downtown Norfolk, Virginia — a 1919 building financed, designed and built by African Americans and one of the oldest surviving theatres of its kind in the United States. Jazz Got Loose treats jazz not only as a musical form but as a cultural movement rooted in New Orleans' Black communities and defined by freedom, resistance, identity and transformation. The call seeks work exploring liberation, resilience, social change, individuality and the courage to push against convention; politically charged, narrative-driven and culturally critical work is welcome, and Black artists and artists whose work reflects the cultural legacy of the Attucks are especially encouraged to apply. Delegate Jackie Hope Glass will jury the exhibition and select up to 50 original works. Any 2-D or relief visual medium is eligible, so photography qualifies, provided pieces do not exceed 50 pounds and arrive exhibition-ready with secure hanging hardware; video and digital work must come with its own display equipment. Artists must be 18 or over with a connection to Hampton Roads, and submit up to three images with title, medium, dimensions, year and a brief description of each work, a bio of up to 250 words and a statement of up to 300 words. There is no entry fee. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, sales enquiries go straight to the artist, and Norfolk Arts takes no commission. The exhibition runs 29 October 2026 to 10 April 2027; artists deliver and collect their own work. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Six-month exhibition at the Attucks Theatre.

item.title: River Margin — Issue 1
item.description: River Margin is a new Australian and international literary journal founded in 2026 by the Melbourne-based visual artist, musician and writer Lana Eileen, and it is assembling its first issue. The focus is ecology, botany and wilderness: the journal was created as a space for overlooked aspects of the natural world — tiny wild-growing plants, threatened rivers, things hidden in the undergrowth. The name refers to the riparian zone, the natural border between water and land, and the editorial position follows from it: River Margin is a space where the liminal, the edge-dwelling, the peripheral and the unnoticed can find a voice. Photographers can submit up to seven images that relate in some way to ecology, botany, the environment, conservation or wilderness areas — rivers and bodies of water, insects, wildlife, fungi, plants, forests, mountains. Both digital and film photography are accepted; AI-generated work is not, and for visual art more broadly the journal excludes digital art as well. Files go by a file-sharing service such as WeTransfer to the journal's submissions address. Submissions are open worldwide and free, and the editors aim to respond within two weeks. The journal is candid that as a new publication compiling its first issue it is not in a position to pay contributors, so the return is publication in Issue 1 alongside poetry, essays, short fiction and creative non-fiction on the same themes. Submissions for the first issue close on 1 November 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in Issue 1.

item.title: Explorations: How We See Things · The Dellora A. Norris Cultural Arts Center
item.description: The Norris Gallery's 2027 juried winter exhibition at the Dellora A. Norris Cultural Arts Center in St. Charles, Illinois. Explorations has no fixed subject: entries should reflect what engages the artist and inspires their exploration — of subject matter, of art processes, of media, or of point of view. Artists may submit up to three original works in any 2D or 3D medium or art process, which places photography squarely within scope; the only medium bar is on reproductions, so no giclées, and no work previously exhibited in the Norris galleries. The entry fee is $35 and is non-refundable. Monetary awards and honourable mentions are presented at the artists' reception. Accepted work cannot be shipped: it must be delivered in person by the artist or a representative on 4 January 2027 and collected on 15 February, which in practice limits the show to artists within reach of the Fox Valley. All accepted work must be for sale and must remain on display for the full run, with the centre retaining 30% commission on anything sold; accepted work may also be posted on the Norris Galleries website as well as hung in the gallery. Entries close on Monday 16 November 2026, artists hear back by Friday 11 December, and the exhibition runs 9 January to 14 February 2027. The Norris is a long-running community arts centre near Chicago with a performance hall and a gallery programme, and it runs a second annual juried show, Watercolor, on a separate cycle. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Building Blocks: What Are We Building With? · St. Charles Arts Council
item.description: A blind-juried open call from the St. Charles Arts Council for an exhibition at its gallery in historic downtown St. Charles, Illinois. The premise is elemental: every creation begins with a single component, whether a stroke of paint, a block of wood or a spark of imagination, and the council asks how the individual components an artist chooses dictate the meaning of the final structure — for the artwork, for a life, or for a community. All art mediums are accepted and three-dimensional and assemblage work is actively encouraged, which leaves photography fully eligible. Artists may enter one or two pieces; the fee is $35 for non-members and $20 for council members, chosen from a tiered drop-down at entry. Work must be original, created within the last seven years, and never previously shown in a St. Charles Arts Council exhibit, and all entries must be for sale. Awards are presented at the opening reception, timed so that every participating artist can arrive: $150 for Best in Show, $75 for second place, $50 for third and further honourable mentions at the judge's discretion. Entries close 11 August 2026; work is dropped off on 31 August, the exhibition runs from early September to 25 October 2026 with an opening reception on the evening of 10 September, and pick-up is 26 October. The council notes it has no storage space, so artists unable to attend drop-off or collection must send someone in their place. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $35 ($20 members). Prize: $150 / $75 / $50 + Exhibition.

item.title: Petite Creations · Gresham Area League for the Arts
item.description: The Gresham Area League for the Arts' winter exhibition, hung in the Gresham Council Chamber Visual Arts Gallery in Oregon over the peak holiday season and mirrored in GALA's online galleries. The brief is scale: two-dimensional work must measure no more than 9 by 9 inches including the frame and no less than 5 by 5, and three-dimensional work must fit inside a 9-inch cube. Within that constraint the league is open across media and names photography directly alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, pottery, fibre art and other 3-D work. Artists may enter up to three pieces for a single $30 submission fee, and GALA retains 20% commission on sales. Preference goes to artists in the greater Gresham area, though the league may widen the pool depending on the number of submissions; in practice the binding constraint is that artists must live within 30 miles of Gresham, because accepted work has to be delivered to the gallery in person. Work featuring nudity or sexual content is not accepted. Entries close 28 October 2026 and the exhibition runs 23 November 2026 to 8 January 2027. — Deadline: October 28, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Presentations of Authorial Projects — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
item.description: The third of the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa's parallel open calls — alongside its photobook dummy exhibition and its self-publishing and small publishers space — this one offers photographers a speaking slot rather than a table. Selected authors present their own photobook project to fair visitors at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico on Rua da Palma, in sessions running across the fair: Friday 27 November between 5:30pm and 7:30pm, and Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November between 11:00am and 12:30pm and again from 2:00pm to 7:30pm. Each presentation runs a maximum of 25 minutes and a projector is available. Pre-registration is through a bilingual Portuguese/English Google Form and closes at 9:00pm on 12 October 2026; the fair's organisation confirms by 6 November whether the presentation will go ahead and at what time. There is no participation fee. The organisers note that authors whose project includes a photobook for sale should also register separately for the Espaço dos Autores e Pequenos Editores, and that dummies can be submitted in parallel for pre-selection in the dummy exhibition — the three calls share a deadline but are entered independently. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Photobook presentation at the fair.

item.title: Small Works, Big Impact · The 203 Art Space
item.description: The 203 Art Space, a contemporary gallery and creative hub that opened in March 2026 on the 5th floor of the Stamford Town Center, invites submissions for its next monthly exhibition, "Small Works, Big Impact." The brief is bold pieces no larger than 24 x 24 inches that leave a lasting impression despite their scale — work where detail, colour, vibrancy and concept carry the memory. Photography is a named accepted medium alongside mixed media, digital, sculpture and painting. Artists may submit one to three pieces. All work must be wired and ready to hang; if stretcher bars are less than an inch and a half deep, the piece must be framed. Selections are announced 21 August and accepted work is dropped off in person at the gallery on 22 and 23 August. The show runs 26 August to 26 September 2026, with an opening reception on Saturday 29 August, 3–5pm. The gallery retains a 30% commission on work sold during the exhibition; the artist receives 70%. Entry is $40 for the first piece and $10 for each additional piece. Note that drop-off and pick-up are in person in Stamford, and no cash award is offered — the exhibition itself is the opportunity. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: $40 (1 piece) + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ANTHOLOGY 3 · Ephemere
item.description: ANTHOLOGY is Ephemere's cyclical curated group exhibition and publication series, and its third volume forms part of the Ephemere Photo Fest 2026 in Tokyo. Exactly nine artists are selected each round — "nine distinct petals of a single flower" — a number chosen so individual narratives complement rather than compete with one another across the gallery walls and the pages of an accompanying photobook. Applicants submit a portfolio of 15 to 20 images; the curatorial team, led by Ephemere founder Anne Murayama and assisted by Alfred Ong, then selects the nine final images that will represent each artist in both the show and the book. Ephemere handles all printing, layout design, framing and installation. ANTHOLOGY 3 runs 17–27 October 2026 on the 3rd floor of Three Space Tokyo. Applying is free, but selected artists pay a strictly non-refundable all-inclusive participation fee — ¥27,500 for Japan-based artists, $275 for visiting artists — covering the 11-day gallery placement, curatorial administration, professional printing and installation, and one complimentary copy of the photobook. Attendance is mandatory: proxy representation is not allowed and selected artists must be physically present in Tokyo on their designated Artist Talk day to give a 10–15 minute presentation alongside their work. Travel and accommodation are the artist's own cost. Two group video meetings in September cover logistics, and artists who join the take-down on 28 October may take their prints home free of charge. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: Free ($275 if selected). Prize: Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Self-Publishing and Small Publishers Space — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
item.description: Alongside its photobook dummy exhibition, the Lisbon Photobook Fair runs a Self-Publishing and Small Publishers Space — the Espaço dos Autores e Pequenos Editores — giving photographers who publish their own work, and the small presses that publish them, a place to sell at the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa, held 27–29 November 2026 at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico on Rua da Palma. The Authors' Space is managed by the fair's own organisation and asks a single one-off contribution rather than taking a cut: €10 covers up to two different titles and €20 covers three or four, in both cases with no limit on the number of copies you bring and, in the organisers' own words, no commission whatsoever on sales. Pre-registration is through a bilingual Portuguese/English Google Form submitted together with a maximum of six photographs of each photobook (72 dpi, 2 MB maximum, named for author and work) sent by WeTransfer to the fair under the subject 'Self-Publishers'. A registration only counts once the form, the images and the contribution have all been received. Pre-registration closes at 21:00 GMT on 12 October 2026, confirmations go out on 23 October, and books must reach the Arquivo Municipal by 16 November, delivered in person Monday to Saturday, 10am–6pm, or by post at the author's own cost; unsold copies are collected from the archive after the fair. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: €10 (up to 2 titles) / €20 (3–4 titles). Prize: Photobook fair sales space.

item.title: Emerald Renaissance: Celebrating 80 Years of Exhibiting Excellence · Philadelphia Chapter of The Links, Incorporated
item.description: A juried fine art exhibition marking the 80th anniversary of the Philadelphia chapter of The Links, Incorporated, the Black women's service organization founded in 1946. The theme asks how Black women — through friendship and service — have used the arts, education and cultural leadership to uplift communities across generations, and invites work that speaks to culture, history, connection and shared responsibility, interpreted through personal, cultural, historical or contemporary perspectives. Photography is explicitly among the eligible media, with painting, mixed media and works on paper. Open to artists living in Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery or Philadelphia counties, Pennsylvania; artists from historically underrepresented and underserved communities are strongly encouraged to apply, and emerging, mid-career and established artists are all welcome. Up to three works at $25 per entry; work must be original, made in the last three to five years, ready to install, at least 24 and no more than 36 inches wide and no more than 72 inches high. The jurors are Adrian J. Moody, gallerist and co-owner of Moody Jones Gallery; Rosalyn 'Roz' J. McPherson of The Roz Group, formerly Senior Vice President for the Science Center at The Franklin Institute; and Shelley R. Sylva, Head of Corporate Citizenship at TD Bank. Artists are notified 19 October 2026 and the exhibition is presented on 14 November 2026 at Founder's Hall, Girard College, alongside a live painting session and auction. All accepted work must be available for acquisition, with sales split 50/50 in favour of the artist; proceeds support the chapter's education, arts, health and mentorship programmes. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $25 per artwork. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Collectives' Hub 2026 · Photo Fringe
item.description: Photo Fringe is a volunteer-led registered charity in Brighton that has run a biennial open-platform photography festival since 2003. The Collectives' Hub has been part of the festival since 2014 and is consistently one of its most visited and critically discussed exhibitions; for the twelfth edition, up to eight photography or lens-based collectives will be selected to build their own shows inside the main gallery at Phoenix Art Space, on view 2 October to 22 November 2026. Work should respond to Future Histories, the theme curating the Main Gallery this year — an invitation to consider how the past keeps configuring and sometimes overshadowing the present, and how what we do now is already writing tomorrow's history. Collectives interpret that freely. A collective needs at least three people, with no upper limit; spaces run between 3.5 and 5 metres wide and are allocated by Photo Fringe producer Ricardo Reverón Blanco and Phoenix curator Laurence Hill. Work can be wall-hung or freestanding, collectives install and de-install themselves with a Photo Fringe technician on hand, and every selected group also makes an online exhibition on photofringe.org. Entry is free: apply by emailing up to 200 words on the proposed exhibition, up to 200 words on the collective, up to 12 JPEGs and a website or Instagram link — video applications in BSL or English and audio applications of up to three minutes are equally welcome. If selected, each collective pays the subsidised Photo Fringe 2026 group registration fee of £150 plus £130 towards production by 2 September, produces its own exhibition, and covers travel and transport; Phoenix Art Space takes 35% commission on sales. Submissions close 11.59pm on Sunday 9 August 2026 and shortlisted collectives hear back on 26 August. — Deadline: August 9, 2026. Fee: Free (£150 group registration + £130 production contribution if selected). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Newhaven Open 26 · Photo Fringe
item.description: A new open exhibition from Photo Fringe, the volunteer-led Brighton charity behind the biennial open-platform photography festival, staged on the top floor of BN9 Marine Workshops in Newhaven — a working-waterfront studio space run by Towner with Newhaven Enterprise Zone and Lewes District Council, with almost 200 square metres of hanging space. Ten solo or group exhibitions will be selected, running 2 to 31 October 2026 alongside the rest of the festival. Work should respond to the 2026 festival theme Feedback Loop, which asks artists to treat photography less as a static record than as part of a continuous exchange: conversations between communities and landscapes, stories circulating across generations, ecological cycles, industrial systems, acts of collaboration, the shifting relationship between artists and audiences. It should also connect meaningfully to Marine Workshops, Newhaven or its communities — the call is open to photographers and lens-based artists in any medium, including installation, moving image, sound and expanded photographic practice, and site-responsive proposals for new or existing work are both welcome. Collectives may apply. Apply free by email with up to 300 words on the proposal, up to 12 JPEGs or a screener link, and a website or Instagram link; BSL, English audio and video applications are accepted. One exhibiting artist receives a jury award of mentorship with Photo Fringe producer Ricardo Reverón Blanco plus an in-depth interview published on the festival site. Selected artists install and de-install their own work with team support, invigilate for at least a day, and pay the subsidised registration fee of £125 solo or £150 group plus a £100 contribution towards exhibition costs by 2 September; Photo Fringe takes 35% commission on sales to cover staffing. Entries close 11.59pm on Sunday 23 August 2026, with notifications on 28 August. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: Free (£125 solo / £150 group registration + £100 exhibition contribution if selected). Prize: Exhibition + Mentorship.

item.title: Medium Gallery Open Call 2027
item.description: Medium Gallery was founded on 8 January 1991 as part of the Academy of Fine Arts and Design in Bratislava, and its programme spans every form of contemporary art the school teaches — photography, painting, intermedia, graphic design, sculpture, applied arts, architecture, design, restoration, textiles and visual communication. For 2027 it is again inviting exhibition projects from students of art fields, beginning and established artists, and curatorial projects, from Slovakia and abroad; the gallery board deliberately balances student presentations against shows by established local and international artists. The 173-square-metre space can be partitioned, a practice begun by former gallery head Jana Kapelová in 2018, so applicants choose one of three configurations: SMALL, the back room, best for compact solo shows; MEDIUM, the two front rooms, for a solo or smaller group show; or LARGE, the whole gallery. Proposals are assessed by a five-person board of three school representatives, the gallery manager and one external member. The gallery covers the space and its running costs, invigilation, technical equipment, plinths and basic installation supplies, transport of works by agreement, graphic design and a print run of posters in the gallery's visual identity, press and social media, photographic documentation of the opening and installation views, the opening itself, and partial help installing; artists cover opening refreshments, their own installation labour, any equipment the gallery cannot supply, and returning the space to its prior state. Applications are free and go by email to the gallery, with a short and detailed project description, chosen space, CVs, an artist portfolio as a single PDF, a preferred exhibition date, an installation plan and any accompanying programme. Final bachelor's and master's theses are not eligible. The deadline is Sunday 16 August 2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: International Mute Photo Festival 2027 — Nature Ate the Pixels · Photonisos Arts & Culture
item.description: Photonisos Arts & Culture, the Samos non-profit behind the East End – Samos Arts Festival, is launching the first International Mute Photo Festival with a single, uncompromising rule: every photograph must be captured and printed on a children's instant thermal camera — the cheap toy that spits low-resolution black-and-white images onto thermal paper. The festival frames this as a deliberate subversion, taking Guy Debord's warning about a world replaced by its own images and answering it with a medium too coarse to flatter anything. The theme, Nature Ate the Pixels, asks for work in which human presence sits inside the natural world rather than above it, split across four categories: Landscape (nature with no human trace), Symbiosis (the body meeting water, earth and flora), Rebirth (nature reclaiming the cityscape) and Future (children discovering the natural world). Post-processing is almost entirely forbidden — you may crop the printed timestamp and white borders and convert to black and white, and nothing else; the lines, marks and noise of the thermal print are treated as the work's core identity, not as faults. Entrants submit high-resolution scans of their original prints, and the jury may ask to see the physical strips to verify the medium. Fifteen adult series and five from the under-18 category are selected, printed and enlarged entirely at the festival's expense, published in a printed catalogue, and shown in July 2027 at the renovated Old Customs Warehouses at Karlovasi Port on Samos. The artist behind the most complete series gets travel and accommodation covered for the opening. Entry is free, and artists retain full copyright. Submissions open 1 September 2026 and close 30 April 2027 at 23:59 EEST; adults send 6 to 9 images with a 250-word statement by email as a single ZIP, and under-18 entries of 5 images must come from a parent or guardian's address with a written consent declaration in the body of the email. — Deadline: April 30, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Food: Ritual and Identity · Metchosin ArtPod
item.description: The artist-run ArtPod on southern Vancouver Island closes its 2026 season with a show about what feeds us. Food is never just food, the curators write — it is material, metaphor, ritual and resource, and it feeds identities, cultures, economies and memories as much as bodies. The call asks for work that traces the visible and invisible systems that sustain or exploit us, from harvest to hunger and feast to waste, and treats food as personal, political, ecological and sensual at once. The guiding question is what it means to be nourished in a time of both abundance and imbalance. The curatorial team is Anna Mar, Pierrette Vezina and Cindy McMath, with Janice Beaudoin jurying. Photography is explicitly welcome under the ArtPod's standing submission guidelines: limited-edition photographs and prints, including giclée, inkjet and archival prints, are accepted in editions of 25 or fewer, and photographs must be taken by the artist and may not reproduce another artist's work. On AI the ArtPod says it is still reflecting, but requires submitted work to represent the artist's own creative vision and authorship. Jurying is blind — the juror sees only the image, the medium and substrate, and an artist statement capped at 1,000 characters. Artists may submit up to three original works; diptychs, triptychs and small series count as one work if shown in a single photograph. Two-dimensional work must not exceed 7 feet high by 5 feet wide. Work must not have been shown in a juried exhibition or commercial gallery on southern Vancouver Island in the past year. Submission is CA$10 per artwork with a further CA$20 hanging fee per accepted work; the ArtPod takes 30% commission and all work must be for sale. The call runs 12 August to 9 October with results on 12 October, and the exhibition runs 23 October to 20 December 2026 with an opening gala on 24 October, 2–4 pm. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: CA$10 per work (CA$20 more if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Truth in Art: A Juried Opportunity for MFA Students · Steffen Thomas Museum of Art
item.description: The Steffen Thomas Museum of Art is a single-artist museum — one of only fourteen in the United States by its own count — built around the work of German-born American painter and sculptor Steffen Thomas. Through its College Connections programme the museum runs this free juried exhibition for MFA students, and the point is as much the apprenticeship as the wall space: selected students work alongside museum mentors on curating, loan forms and condition reports, art installation, exhibition promotion and public speaking, so the show doubles as a first practical education in how a museum actually mounts an exhibition. The top three Best in Show selections receive a monetary award. Entry is free. Submissions close 29 August 2026 and the exhibition runs 26 September to 21 November 2026 in the museum's West Gallery in Buckhead, Georgia, in Morgan County about ten minutes from historic Madison. — Deadline: August 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: PLAYFUL · Arc Studios & Gallery
item.description: Arc is a mixed-use art centre on Folsom Street in San Francisco's South of Market district, founded in 2010 by four artist partners and running three galleries alongside ten artist studios. Its 2027 national juried call opens with Claes Oldenburg — "I am for the art of the underwear and the art of taxicabs" — and asks for work that embodies the playful spirit: light-hearted, lively, spontaneous, full of fun, amusement and wit. That can arrive as bright colour, whimsical typography, funny imagery or sly innuendo, and the gallery specifically names spontaneous street photography alongside interactive works that invite audience participation and works that hold on to child-like wonder and game-play. Photography is one of the accepted categories; jewellery, video, film, performance, installation and anything needing an external power source are not. The juror is Jennifer Farris, who has run STUDIO Gallery in San Francisco with her husband, artist Rab Terry, for over two decades. Three works chosen by the juror for the most imaginative reading of the theme receive a $250 check, a juror's award ribbon, a recognition certificate and the show catalogue; every selected work, gallery and online alike, appears in that catalogue. Entry is $35 for one to three images, with a maximum of two entries per artist, and the call is open to artists residing in the United States. Two-dimensional work is capped at 60 by 40 inches including frame, and accepted work must arrive ready to hang with plexi rather than glass. Submissions close 29 March 2027, notifications go out 16 April, and the exhibition runs 19 June to 17 July 2027 at 1246 Folsom Street. — Deadline: March 29, 2027. Fee: $35 per entry (1–3 works). Prize: $250 awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Living Image 2026/2027 · The Halide Project
item.description: The Halide Project is a nonprofit darkroom and gallery on North 2nd Street in Philadelphia, and Living Image is its annual juried exhibition of traditional and historic photographic processes — the show it builds its year around. The 2026/27 edition is juried by Amanda Smith, who founded A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas fifteen years ago and has run more than 200 juried and curated exhibitions there, alongside jury work for All About Photo, Analogue Forever, Dodho, Texas Photographic Society, the International Photography Hall of Fame and Critical Mass. Selected work hangs at The Halide Project gallery from 5 December 2026 to 17 January 2027 and is published in a printed catalogue; every selected artist receives a copy. One Grand Prize winner takes $250 and a slot to show a body of work in The Halide Project's annual Spring Invitational, with further sponsored prizes announced later. The medium gate is strict and specific: work must be made using traditional, pre-digital photographic printing — silver gelatin, c-prints, instant film, platinum/palladium, cyanotype, gum bichromate, wet plate collodion and other alternative and historic processes. Analog prints made from digital negatives are eligible; inkjet prints and digital c-prints are not, even if shot on film. Open to artists 18 or older in any country. Entry is $40 for up to three works and $10 for each additional, to a maximum of ten, with a $5 discount off the total for members. Accepted work must arrive framed and wired to professional standards by 7 November and must not exceed 30 inches in any dimension including the frame; artists cover shipping both ways, and the gallery retains a 25% commission on sales. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $40 (1–3 works), $10 each additional. Prize: $250 + Exhibition + Printed catalogue.

item.title: INSIDE / OUTSIDE · Second Street Gallery
item.description: Second Street Gallery, founded in 1973 and the oldest nonprofit contemporary art space in Central Virginia, is running a juried regional exhibition for artists living and working in the Commonwealth of Virginia. INSIDE / OUTSIDE asks for work that sits on the line between interior and exterior worlds — home and environment, personal space and public life, private memory and shared history. The gallery invites broad interpretation: Virginia's natural landscape, the built environment, domestic interiors, social and cultural histories, or the psychological boundaries between inside and out. The juror is Kristen Chiacchia, Second Street's Executive Director and Chief Curator, an art historian whose curatorial practice centres on gender bias in the contemporary art market and on artists' ties to subcultural movements; she has curated more than 67 solo shows and 34 group exhibitions at the gallery and published nine catalogues. First place takes $300 plus a solo exhibition in the gallery's Dové space from 2 June to 21 July 2028; second is $200 and third is $100, with up to three honourable mentions at the juror's discretion. Accepted media are painting, works on paper, sculpture, photography and mixed media — no video, installation, performance, sound or AI-generated work. Work must have been made in the last three years and must not have been shown in Charlottesville in the preceding year. Applications open 15 August 2026 and close 15 November; artists are notified 15 January 2027, work is delivered in May, and the show runs 4 June to 16 July 2027 with a First Friday opening. All exhibited work must be available for purchase and the gallery retains a 50% commission. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35 ($20 members). Prize: $300 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: RED — Juried Exhibition · Lawrence Arts Center
item.description: Red tape, red flag, seeing red, painting the town red — the Lawrence Arts Center wants to know what it means to represent the colour red, and leaves the reading entirely to the artist. The theme can be taken as intense emotion or as warning, or turned toward flowers, birds and hearts; the call explicitly encourages both established and emerging artists. Submissions are open to any medium within the size limit, which is 24 inches in any direction including frame, and selected work is not required to be for sale. The juror is Travis Millard, the artist, musician and founder of Fudge Factory Comics, with twenty years of self-published zines and gallery shows behind him and illustration work for Playboy, The Hollywood Reporter, Mad, Wired and record covers for Dinosaur Jr and Kurt Vile. Prizes are $1,000 for first, $500 for second and $250 for third. The Arts Center is a long-running nonprofit in downtown Lawrence, Kansas, with three exhibition galleries, a 300-seat theatre and seven visual arts studios. Entries go through the SlideRoom portal, which opened 1 August and closes 25 September; a maximum of three original works may be entered for $25, one JPEG per piece under 5MB. AI artwork is not permissible. Notifications go out between 5 and 9 October, work is delivered 10–21 October, the opening reception and awards are on 30 October, and the show closes 12 December 2026. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $25 (up to 3 works). Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Remember You Must Live: On Life, Loss, and Impermanence · Guilford Art Center
item.description: Guilford Art Center — a nonprofit school, gallery and shop on the Connecticut shoreline, whose gallery shows contemporary American art and craft year-round and free to the public — is assembling a memento mori show for its October slot. Remember You Must Live asks artists to sit with an inevitable phase of life rather than sensationalise it: not fear or spectacle, but cycles, transitions and the preciousness of what is here. The call is open to artists in Connecticut and the wider New England region, working in all physical mediums, and there is no entry fee. Each artist submits two works that respond to the theme, emailed with the completed submission form to the Center's exhibitions coordinator by 30 August; the in-house exhibitions team notifies artists of their status by Sunday 13 September. Accepted work is received 4 and 5 October, the exhibition runs 9 to 30 October 2026 with an opening reception on 10 October, and pick-up is 31 October to 1 November. Work must arrive in exhibition condition with identifying paperwork, and anything not for sale must be marked NFS with a stated insurance value. Guilford Art Center retains a 40% commission on sales, with cheques mailed within thirty days of the close of the show, and insures exhibited work for 50% of the artist's stated retail value against fire, theft and breakage from receiving to removal. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SATURATION · projectART
item.description: projectART is a 501(c)(3) arts education nonprofit in Wimberley, Texas, running youth programmes, artist mentorships and a gallery — ARTSPACE on River Road — for rural Central Texas. SATURATION is its next group exhibition, a show about vivid colour, visual intensity and the idea of fullness. The call wants bold palettes, rich surfaces and immersive compositions, but equally work that treats saturation as a concept: abundance, excess, density, emotion, sensory overload. It also invites readings of saturation as a social, psychological, cultural or environmental condition — information overload, consumerism, identity, memory, being engulfed by a feeling, the point at which intensity transforms perception. All visual art media are welcome and submission is free. The exhibition opens with a reception on 9 October 2026 and stays on view at ARTSPACE through 9 January 2027, a three-month run. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Call for Solo Exhibition Proposals · St. Louis Artists' Guild
item.description: The St. Louis Artists' Guild has been showing regional work since 1886 and runs a free gallery on North Jackson Avenue in Clayton, just west of the city. Its open call for proposals is for solo exhibitions, from emerging and established artists alike, working in all media — a rare thing to find with no submission fee attached. Selected artists show in either the Guild's curated gallery or its ramp gallery; floor plans for both are published alongside the call so proposals can be pitched to the space. Applicants must live within a 150-mile radius of St. Louis, be 18 or older, and have a website of their own (Instagram and Facebook pages do not count). One proposal per artist. Two or more artists may collaborate on a proposal or pitch a group exhibition, but it must be submitted under a single name. Anyone who has already had a solo exhibition at the Guild must wait five years before showing again. Proposals go in through the Guild's Google Form by midnight on 5 September 2026. — Deadline: September 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Galleries Call for Artists · City of San Ramon
item.description: The City of San Ramon, 35 miles east of San Francisco, programmes five gallery spaces and this call fills their month-long exhibition slots for the whole of 2027. The venues vary in scale and in what they can take: the Dougherty Station Community Arts Center hangs 30-plus pieces across up to 115 linear feet of 2D and 3D; the Lindsay Dirkx Brown Gallery takes 25 to 30 pieces over 100 linear feet, also 2D and 3D; San Ramon City Hall holds 30-plus 2D pieces across 125 linear feet; the Alcosta Senior & Community Center takes 20 to 25 2D pieces; and the San Ramon Library shows 10 to 15. The city says the programme is deliberately open to artists at any age and any stage, and accepts both solo and group proposals, so long as the applicant has a body of at least ten completed works. Accepted media are two-dimensional or three-dimensional work with the sole exception of film, so photography qualifies; AI-generated work does not, work already shown in a San Ramon gallery in 2025 or 2026 cannot be repeated, and the city bars nudity, violence and what it calls otherwise inappropriate imagery or themes. There is no application fee — selected artists pay a $50 exhibition fee, due 30 November. Applications are made through CaFE with five image samples, an artist statement and a resume; the portal window runs 10 August to 27 September. The Arts Advisory Committee reviews on 21 October and notifications go out 2 November. Work may be sold during the run, with a 20% sales commission payable to the city. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: Free ($50 exhibition fee if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Alternative Aesthetic: Chance at the Margins · PhotoSC
item.description: PhotoSC is a non-profit photography gallery in Columbia, South Carolina, built around a continuing dialogue about photography and the photographic canon. Marking photography's 200 years of experimentation, The Alternative Aesthetic: Chance at the Margins goes looking for the accident and the sleight of hand — the idea that chance has sat at the heart of photographic and scientific discovery from the very beginning, and that the non-traditional method has always been the alternative to the cultural order of photography. The call seeks historical techniques, photosensitive chemicals and unusual materials, and the textures, colours and effects that are impossible with standard digital or silver gelatin work; experimentation is explicitly encouraged. The juror is Michael Kirchoff, Editor-in-Chief of Analog Forever Magazine, founding editor of Catalyst: Interviews, an ongoing juror for Photolucida's Critical Mass and a former board member of APA/LA. Photographers may submit up to five works for $35, with submissions open from 5 August to 13 September 2026 and accepted artists notified by 4 October. Accepted work must be printed no smaller than 8×10 inches and no larger than 16×20, framed and ready to hang, and delivered by the 23 October receipt-of-work date on the call timeline (a line of prose lower down the same page still says 30 September, which predates the 4 October notification). The exhibition opens 29 October at 918 Lady Street, Columbia, with a reception the same evening, and hangs until 29 November 2026. Sales are encouraged at a 40/60 gallery/artist split; photographers retain copyright. No AI-generated imagery is accepted. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Seed Prize for Emerging Photographers 2026 · National Emerging Art Prize
item.description: The National Emerging Art Prize was founded in 2021 to give Australia's most promising emerging visual artists a national platform, and in 2025 it expanded into contemporary photography with a dedicated category — The Seed Prize for Emerging Photographers, sponsored by Seed Funds Management, now in its second year. The winner receives a $10,000 acquisitive cash prize, a solo exhibition at The Garden Gallery presented by Michael Reid Northern Beaches in 2027, and mentoring sessions with NEAP curator Amber Creswell Bell and the Michael Reid directors. NEAP is curated by Amber Creswell Bell, a writer and curator known for championing emerging Australian artists across a run of best-selling books on Australian art; she sits on the selection panel and works with the selected artists to curate the finalists' exhibition. The 2026 panel includes artists Tom Polo and Tamara Dean, Head On Photo Festival founder Moshe Rosenzveig OAM, Belle editor-in-chief Tanya Buchanan, Good Weekend senior writer Katrina Strickland, Decus founder Alexandra Donohoe Church, and collectors Edwina Bartholomew and Nicole Redden. There is no theme. The category is open to film and digital photographs presented as still, two-dimensional works, completed in 2025 or 2026. Prints must be at least 20cm square and no larger than 100cm on the longest side, editioned no higher than 15 (8 + 2AP recommended), and priced no higher than $3,000 unframed; finalists send work in tubes and it is exhibited unframed, pinned directly to the gallery wall, with NEAP retaining 50% of any sale. Artists must reside primarily in Australia and count as emerging — that is, not represented by a major commercial gallery; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists are encouraged to apply. There is no limit on entries per artist, but each work is submitted separately at $35. Finalists are announced 1 October and exhibited 29 October to 11 November 2026 at The Garden Gallery in Sydney's Royal Botanic Garden, with all work for sale. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: A$35 per work. Prize: A$10,000 + Solo exhibition + Mentoring.

item.title: Windows on the World · Click! Photography Festival
item.description: Click! Photography Festival turns downtown Raleigh into a month-long photography city every October, spreading exhibitions, talks and screenings across Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. Windows on the World is its storefront show: selected photographs are printed by the festival and installed in and around the shop windows of City Market, the historic brick market district in downtown Raleigh, so the work is met by people walking past rather than by gallery visitors. The theme is JOY, and the call asks what joy looks like to you — a fleeting smile, a quiet landscape, a family celebration, an unexpected encounter, a moment of personal triumph. All genres are welcome, from documentary and street photography to portraits, landscapes, abstract and experimental imagery, and all photographic processes are accepted: alternative, film or digital. The call is open to photographers of all levels, from emerging talents to seasoned professionals, and international submissions are accepted. Entry is $45 for up to five images. Artists do not ship work: everything selected is printed and displayed by the festival, with the possibility of a projection event on First Friday. The exhibition runs 1–31 October 2026 with an opening reception on Friday 2 October, and images not selected for the outdoor Plein Air exhibition are eligible for a travelling slide show presented around the Triangle through October. AI-generated images are not eligible. — Deadline: August 24, 2026. Fee: $45/5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Click! Plein Air
item.description: Click! Plein Air is the flagship outdoor exhibition of the Click! Photography Festival, the month-long October festival spread across Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill in North Carolina. For 2026 it moves from Moore Square, where the 2025 edition showed 35 photographers, to Dix Park — the 300-acre former state hospital campus that is now Raleigh's largest public park — where photographs are shown in the open air rather than on gallery walls. There is no set theme: photographers submit into open categories, and the festival is looking for striking, engaging work that holds up in front of a broad public audience outdoors. The festival's own page lists seven — abstract, documentary, landscape, people, creatures, street photography and still life — while the Smarter Entry form shows six, with portrait in place of people and creatures, so check the list when you upload. The call is open to photographers of all levels and to all photographic processes, alternative, film or digital, with international submissions accepted. Entry is $45 for up to five images, each of which must be titled. The juror is Jerome De Perlinghi. Jury selections are made by 6 September, the exhibition runs 1–31 October 2026, and the opening reception is on First Friday, 2 October. Images not selected for the outdoor exhibition remain eligible for a travelling slide show presented at venues throughout the Triangle during October. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $45/5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SELF PORTRAITS 2026 · Matt Ford Studio
item.description: Matt Ford Studio is a photographer-run gallery and studio in Hackney Downs Studios, east London, whose programme leans toward sexuality, gender, identity and fashion. SELF PORTRAITS 2026 is its winter open call, exhibition and photo book, put together by Matt Ford after he began making self-portraits as a way of working through his own fears about AI, politics and the future of an artistic career, and became interested in self-portraiture itself — as vanity, as creativity, as self-expression, or simply as a record of where you are in your life. The call invites photographers worldwide to reflect on what it means to be human in the second quarter of the 21st century. Anyone 18 or over from any country may enter, at any level of skill, and both digital and analogue work is welcome — disposable cameras, phones and high-end DSLRs alike — along with collage and experimental work that still involves some element of self-portrait. Digitally enhanced images are accepted; AI-generated images are not. Judging for finalists and winners is done by the editors of ZERO.NINE Magazine. The winner receives £500 cash, the cover of the SELF PORTRAITS photo book, an 'On The Radar' feature in ZERO.NINE and a feature about their work; all semi-finalists appear in the photo book at no extra cost, and finalists are shown in the exhibition at the studio. Entry is £13 for the first photograph and £6 for each one after; if you reach the exhibition a further £20 per photograph shown covers printing (arranged with theprintspace) and exhibition admin, or you may send your own print at your own postage cost. Semi-finalists are announced 9 November, the book launch, private view and winners announcement is 10 December, and the exhibition is open to the public 11–14 December 2026. Work is for sale during the show, with 75% to the artist. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: £13 for 1 image, £6 each additional (£20 per print if selected). Prize: £500 + Exhibition + Photobook.

item.title: Liquida Winter Edition 2026 — Single Photo
item.description: Liquida Photofestival is the photography strand of Paratissima, the independent contemporary art event that has run in Turin since 2005 and is now one of the anchors of Turin Art Week. Its Winter Edition is the autumn spin-off of the main April festival, curated by Liquida's artistic director Laura Tota — an independent curator who has worked on Paratissima's photography programme since 2017 and is Exhibition Coordinator at PhEST, Photolux and Cortona On The Move. Single Photo is a new section for 2026: rather than a project, it asks for individual frames. Each entrant may submit between one and five photographs, which need not belong to the same body of work or even to the same line of research, and there is no set theme — the point is to leave photographers the widest possible margin of expression. Ten winning shots are chosen and shown as a collective exhibition inside the Liquida Winter Edition section, with each selected image coming from a different artist. The €25 participation fee is the only cost: Paratissima covers production, transport, shipping, installation and de-installation of the selected works, and the fee also includes the exhibition layout, wall captions, inclusion in the official ISBN catalogue, an artist badge and support for online and on-site sales. The catalogue itself is optional at €20 a copy. The festival runs 30 October – 1 November 2026 at the Real Collegio Carlo Alberto in Moncalieri, just outside Turin; the 2025 edition drew more than 20,000 visitors. Results are announced 12 September. Note that Liquida's separate Exhibition call, for full projects, works on a paid-wall-space model and is not this call. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Thin Air Magazine Issue 33 — The Oasis
item.description: Thin Air is a print literary and arts magazine produced by graduate students in the MFA programme at Northern Arizona University in Flagstaff, and it is reading visual art for its 33rd print issue, themed 'The Oasis'. The editors take the dictionary definition — a fertile green area in an arid region; something that provides refuge, relief or pleasant contrast — and push at it: in a turbulent and at times desolate world, what is your oasis, where do you seek shelter, and what spaces sustain you? They are equally interested in the conditions that produce an oasis, since one can only exist when surrounded by a severe lack of something crucial to survival — so what is your desert, and what drives you to look for relief? The call also asks whether an oasis can be a form of resistance, thinking of the sanctuaries that form in the midst of violence, fear and escalating political tension. For this issue the editors are specifically looking for art, photography and comics that represent the notion of the oasis, with an interest in pieces that work as full-page spreads as well as graphic narratives and poetry comics; outsider art is always welcome, as is anything that surprises or subverts expectations. Colour submissions are open, with particular interest in high-contrast pieces that capture the shades and hues of the oasis. Photographers may send up to five pieces at a minimum of 300dpi with a short description of each work and a two to five sentence bio. Submitting visual art is free — the written-genre categories carry a $3 reading fee that visual art does not — and only unpublished work is considered, though simultaneous submissions are encouraged. Reading begins in August each year and runs until the deadline. One restriction to note: Thin Air does not accept work from anyone affiliated with Northern Arizona University within the last seven years. — Deadline: October 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Rawhead Issue 04 — Visual Art
item.description: Rawhead is an independent online journal of art and literature named after one of the folkloric bogeymen used to frighten children into obedience — a deliberate choice, since the editors read monsters as mirrors that force us to confront realities more disturbing than whatever lurks in the dark, and read art as a form of resistance. It is not a horror publication, but it is interested in work that unsettles through emotional depth, sharp craft and surprising clarity. Rawhead is open for its fourth issue across poetry, visual art, fiction, creative nonfiction and hybrid work; submissions considered for Issue 04 may also be held for Issue 05. The visual art category takes three to ten pieces in any medium, explicitly including photography alongside illustration, digital collage, mixed media, painting and sculpture, uploaded as high-quality images of at least 1500px. The art editor is looking for work that explores the delicate threshold between fear and beauty — not horror or gore, but work that dances along the edges of heightened emotion, citing Louise Bourgeois, Francis Bacon, Man Ray, Joseba Eskubi, Anna Weyant and Jinyoung Yu as touchstones. Each issue Rawhead selects at least one outstanding artist and one standout writer for its Editor's Spotlight, a $100 award; every accepted piece is considered. Submission is free and the journal states it is fully committed to always offering free submissions, with optional paid expedited and priority response tiers that have no bearing on editorial decisions. Simultaneous submissions are accepted, and AI-generated content is not. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + $100.

item.title: Photobooks in Dialogue · Centrum för fotografi
item.description: Centrum för fotografi (CFF), Sweden's member organisation for photographers, is calling for photobooks and zines for an exhibition in Gothenburg staged with Fotobok Gbg as part of Fotobok Fest. The curators are looking for photo-based publications in which dialogue, collaboration or exchange are central: an exchange of ideas between two photographers, between an artist and an archive, between image and text, or the close interplay of artist, designer and publisher. They describe it as a ping-pong match, where ideas bounce from one side to the other in fine balance without ever falling off the table — books and zines where the exchange between several voices is fundamental and has shaped the work from the ground up. The exhibition runs 25–27 September 2026 at the CFF gallery on Bangatan 10 in Gothenburg, with support from the City of Gothenburg and the Swedish Photographers' Association. Publications from anywhere in the world are welcome, but shipping to Sweden is at the applicant's own cost; books must arrive by 22 September. Applications are free and consist of a single PDF of no more than 10 MB containing a CV of up to two pages, a presentation of the publication of up to 300 words in Swedish or English, and 10–15 pages from the book. Selected participants are notified at the end of August. After the exhibition you can either donate your publication to the Hasselblad Foundation Library in Gothenburg or have it returned at CFF's expense. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Legacy Lives Here II · Project Row Houses
item.description: Project Row Houses, the community arts organisation founded in 1993 in Houston's Third Ward, invites artists aged 60 and over to submit work for the second edition of Legacy Lives Here, a multimedia exhibition celebrating the artistic voices of elders, wisdom-keepers and culture-shapers. The organisers are looking for work that reflects personal histories, cultural memory and the ongoing act of passing down knowledge through art, and the show is open to a wide range of mediums. Submissions close 11:59pm on Friday 28 August 2026 and selected artists are notified by the first week of September. The exhibition is on view in PRH's Community Gallery from 17 September to 17 October 2026. Applications are made through SlideRoom and there is no entry fee. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Sensory Seduction Volume 3 — Into the Void
item.description: Sensory Seduction is a Sydney-based independent print magazine and creative platform covering art, literature, music and culture, now open for its third volume, 'Into the Void: Exploration and Discovery'. The issue embraces all aspects of the unknown and invites work interpreting exploration and discovery in the contributor's own way — going on a journey, doing something for the first time, expansion, travel, investigating a mystery, emigration and immigration, unexpected detours, a chance encounter, embracing a new culture, taking a risk, a transitional period, getting lost, leaving your comfort zone, uncovering a secret. The magazine publishes original, unpublished work across disciplines including photography, digital art, collage, film stills and editorial work alongside essays, interviews, poetry and reviews; existing work is welcome as long as it has not been published before and fits the theme. Photographers and visual artists may submit up to six images with an artist statement and/or captions for each image, and hybrid submissions combining writing and images are accepted. Submission is free, via the magazine's online form, and every submission receives a response. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: FIGURES Mentorship & Dummy Book Program 2026/2027
item.description: FIGURES, the Slow & Contemporary Photography platform behind the FIG001 book, is running its mentorship and dummy book programme for a second year, and is looking specifically for projects at the very earliest stage of creation — you do not need to show a single finished picture of the project to apply, and projects that are already too advanced will not be considered. Program winners get twelve monthly 1.5-hour one-to-one online sessions with founder and editor-in-chief Nicolas Blanchadell, covering every phase from deepening the initial concept through production, picture editing and sequencing; a renowned guest artist/curator joins for one mid-programme session, and a professional art-book graphic designer steps in at the end to finalise the cover and the more demanding pages. Each winner leaves with a printed dummy book plus the ready-to-print PDF and all supporting material. The number of selections scales with entries: for every 150 valid submissions FIGURES picks one program winner plus ten further projects for a one-hour individual review. All photographic practices are welcome — documentary, portrait, street, experimental, fashion — as are mixed-media projects where photography is central to the process or makes up at least half the final work. Entry is €10, or free with the discounted purchase of the FIG001 issue at €25; no further fees are asked of selected artists, and applicants facing financial hardship are invited to write to FIGURES directly. If fewer than 150 valid applications arrive, the programme is cancelled and €10 entrants are refunded in full. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: €10 (or €25 with FIG001 issue). Prize: Mentorship and dummy book.

item.title: New Mexico Blue Bus Shelter Art · New Mexico Arts
item.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme, working with the North Central Regional Transit District's Art in Transit programme, is commissioning artists to create digital artwork to be printed onto perforated steel panels at three Blue Bus shelters in Taos, Española and Santa Fe. Selected artists create an original work — or digitise existing non-digital work — to fit a two- or three-panel shelter, each panel roughly 53 by 77 inches; all printing and installation is handled by NCRTD. The organisers ask for artwork that speaks to the local culture and community: cultural homelands, local languages, landscapes and agricultural practices, the diversity of lifeways, traditions and landmarks, and the artist's own lived experience and connection to the area. This is a request for qualifications, not a proposal call — do not make new work for it; submit up to ten images of completed artwork that demonstrate your style and technique, ideally digital work or work with local themes, plus an artist statement and answers on your transportation story and your connection to Northern New Mexico. Artists are paid $5,000 per completed artwork, inclusive of all fees and expenses. Entry is free. Open to all artists working in New Mexico, with preference given to those living in or with strong ties to Taos, Rio Arriba and Santa Fe counties; employees and family of employees of NMDCA or NCRTD are excluded. Selection is by the Art in Transit Committee, drawn from representatives across Northern New Mexico including Rio Arriba, Santa Fe, Taos and Los Alamos counties, Ohkay Owingeh and Taos Pueblo. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 commission.

item.title: Louvre Unbound Magazine — Celebration Edition
item.description: A one-off anniversary edition marking Louvre Unbound's first year, published alongside an international event in Spain held with Luka Gallery for the inauguration of the gallery's new space inside the Castillo de Santiago, expected to draw 300–400 invited guests including curators, collectors, European press and cultural professionals. Selected artists are published in the Celebration Edition and also receive a two-month virtual exhibition, two months of promotion across the magazine's social channels, worldwide digital publication, global print-on-demand distribution via Peecho and Lulu, and a place on the printed event flyers handed to guests throughout the celebration. Submissions are open to visual artists worldwide working in any medium, photography included; submit up to four artworks through the magazine's Google Form. Submitting is free — participation fees apply only on acceptance, and for this edition alone they are quoted in euros: €89 for returning artists and €115 for new artists, covering a four-page featured-artist spread with one artwork per page plus contact links. Louvre Unbound states it is a non-profit platform and that the fee supports editorial work, design, printing and distribution. The edition will only be published if a minimum number of participating artists is reached; if it is cancelled, all registered artists are refunded in full. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free (€89–€115 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: UNFOLD — Cambridge Photography Gallery
item.description: Cambridge Photography Gallery's first annual physical exhibition, bringing together artists invited from its previous online shows alongside new voices found through this open call. Rather than setting a narrow theme, the gallery asks how your photography unfolds — as a story, a memory, a place, a relationship, an identity or a way of seeing. Some projects reveal themselves slowly while others leave questions unanswered; some look outward, others inward. Singles and series are both welcome and there is no right or wrong interpretation. Selected works are printed and presented as part of the group exhibition in Cambridge, UK, running 9 to 11 October 2026, and each participating artist receives a dedicated post on the gallery's Instagram and a digital certificate of participation. Submission is by email and free; a £30 participation fee applies only if your work is selected. For the selection stage files can be any size, format or orientation; selected artists are then asked for high-resolution files suitable for printing, around 300 ppi and at least 3000 pixels on the longest side. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free (£30 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: HALFTONE Print Fair 2026 · PhotoIreland
item.description: The 12th edition of HALFTONE, PhotoIreland's annual print fair at The Library Project in Dublin's Temple Bar, running 28 November 2026 to 24 January 2027. Works are displayed salon-style and sold both at the venue and online at thelibraryproject.ie; the fair has raised almost €100,000 for artists since 2015 and supported the practice of over 800 participating artists, with sales to private, corporate and public collections. Applications are open to fine art printers, illustrators, designers, photographers and all visual artists and creatives, for works produced from 2024 onwards using any print technique — screenprint, stencil, risography, lithography, etching, inkjet printing and more — without any limitation of approach or concept. Submissions may include up to 10 artworks, with two images per work: the print itself and a photograph or mock-up showing it framed or mounted as it would be displayed. All submitted works must be available for sale. The gallery takes a 40% commission, which should be built into the price you submit, and artists invoice for the remaining 60% after the fair; PhotoIreland adds 13.5% VAT on top of the submitted price. Selected artists are contacted by 2 November 2026 and deliver work between 3 and 15 November, with unsold work collected 25 to 31 January 2027. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: €10 (free for International Centre for the Image members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Southwest Artists Series Purchase Initiative · New Mexico Arts
item.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme buys artwork outright for publicly accessible buildings across the state — amphitheatres, community centres, courthouses, educational institutions, fire stations, healthcare facilities, libraries, recreation complexes, rest areas and senior centres among them. The 2026 Southwest Artists Series Purchase Initiative aims to diversify the state collection by purchasing work from artists at every stage of their careers, and all media in all genres are considered; New Mexico Arts names photography explicitly among the mediums it accepts, alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, mosaic, graphic arts, etching, lithography, silkscreen, textile, fibre, wood, metal, glass, mixed media, collage and assemblage. Work must be durable, permanent, low-maintenance and compliant with ADA guidelines once installed, and suitable for interior or exterior display. The programme seeks artwork in the $5,000–$50,000 range, and the price must be all-inclusive: materials, labour, museum-quality framing under Plexiglas, security hangers, delivery, installation, insurance, taxes, commissions and both written and professional photographic documentation of the work. Since its inception in 1986 AIPP has placed more than 3,000 works of art across all 33 New Mexico counties, amounting to over $21 million paid directly to artists. Open to artists who reside in New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, Colorado, Oklahoma or Texas, and to galleries located in those states, which may submit on behalf of any artist they represent regardless of that artist's residency. A statewide Submission Review Committee of artists, arts professionals and community leaders scores applications, and the selected pool is then shown to local committees for purchase consideration. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$50,000 purchase.

item.title: Wellcome Photography Prize 2027 · Wellcome
item.description: Wellcome's biennial photography prize returns for 2027, open to everyone, everywhere, and free to enter. The prize brings photography and scientific imaging together around health and science: discovery research, mental health, infectious disease, and climate and health. There are three categories — Striking solo photography (a single photograph), A storytelling series (3–5 photographs), and The marvels of scientific and medical imaging (a single image made with a scientific or medical imaging technique). Each category winner receives £10,000, and a further 22 entries across the three categories are awarded £1,000 each; the prize draws extensive international media coverage and image makers may be invited to showcase their work at events. Eligible disciplines include documentary, clinical, studio and still-life photography, close-up photography and photomacrography, microscopy, and medical imaging such as CT, PET, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound and thermography, as well as new and emerging biomedical imaging technologies. Illustration, moving image and AI-generated images are not accepted. Images must have been taken after 31 December 2021 and submitted at print resolution. Judges weigh creativity and visual impact, storytelling and relevance, and technical excellence — the story behind an image counts as much as the image. Wellcome also publishes ethical storytelling guidelines developed with Eh!woza. Entries opened 14 July 2026; the top 25 entries and the winners are announced in summer 2027. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £10,000 per category + 22 × £1,000.

item.title: Open Call for Emerging Artists · Elliott Gallery
item.description: Elliott Gallery in Amsterdam is shifting its open-call programme away from exhibition proposals and towards early-career photographers: recent graduates of universities and photography courses, current students, and self-taught photographers in the early stages of their careers, worldwide. The gallery is explicit that it is not looking for flawless, finished portfolios but for fresh voices, raw talent, authenticity and potential. There is no set theme; the gallery looks for a distinct perspective and a genuine passion for the medium, and accepts photography only. The prize is a personalised mentorship with the Elliott Gallery curatorial team — three 60-minute one-to-one sessions over three months covering how to refine an artistic identity and conceptual approach through intensive portfolio reviews, how to navigate the fine art market, price work, write statements and approach galleries, and how to curate work for digital and physical spaces, with the distinct potential for further collaboration such as digital exhibitions, group shows and print sales. Shortlisted artists also receive exposure across the gallery's website and social channels to its base of fine art photography collectors. Applicants submit a single public link to a folder or online portfolio plus a statement of up to 500 words, via Google Forms. Applications opened 24 July 2026 and close 9 August; the shortlist is announced 14 August and the winner on 21 August 2026. The €25 fee covers administration costs. Elliott Gallery is a physical gallery at Tussen de Bogen 91 and complies with the Gallery Fair Practice Code. — Deadline: August 9, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Art Hop 2026 · Hill Country Arts Focus
item.description: Art Hop is a statewide juried exhibition run by Hill Country Arts Focus, a 501(c)(3) founded in 2007 to promote the arts in the northern Hill Country of central Texas. The 2026 edition runs the whole of October in Georgetown's historic downtown district, with selected work shown at the Georgetown Public Library and Lamppost Coffee, both just off the courthouse Square. Photography is one of six judged categories, alongside 2-D Representational, 2-D Abstract, 3-D Representational, 3-D Abstract and Digital Art; the photography category covers camera-generated photographic images. Awards run to $1,000 for Best in Show plus cash or prizes totalling almost $4,000 across the individual categories, announced at the reception ceremony. Judging happens in two rounds — online in late August, then in person before the exhibit opens, which determines placements and cash awards. Entry is $45 for up to three artworks or $55 for four or five, with a limit of five entries per artist, submitted through EntryThingy. Wall pieces including photography may be up to 48 inches on any side including the frame and must arrive ready to install with professional hardware. The call is open to any artist aged 16 or older residing in Texas. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $45 (up to 3 works), $55 (4–5). Prize: $1,000 Best in Show + category awards.

item.title: 110th Annual Open Juried Show · New Rochelle Art Association
item.description: The New Rochelle Art Association has run an annual juried show since 1912, when its first exhibition celebrated the opening of the city's new library and included work by sculptor Robert Aitken, painters G. Glenn Newell, Remington Schuyler and A.G. Heaton, and illustrators Norman Rockwell, Joseph C. Leyendecker and Victor Forsythe. The 110th edition is open to all artists 18 and over, with Photography one of the judged categories alongside Oil/Acrylic, Water Media, Graphics/Pastel, Mixed Media and Sculpture/Fine Craft. A minimum of $2,500 in cash awards is distributed across the categories. Each artist may submit up to two entries for a single fee of $35 ($30 for members); acceptance into the show automatically brings NRAA membership. All 2-D work must be suitably framed at least 0.75 inches deep — gallery-wrapped canvas is acceptable — wired and ready to hang, with no sawtooth hooks, and must not exceed 36 × 48 inches including the outside edge of the frame. Work is hand delivered rather than shipped. The exhibition runs 28 September to 1 November 2026 in the Lumen Winter Gallery at New Rochelle Public Library, open daily with library hours, with a reception on Sunday 18 October during New Rochelle's Arts Fest. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $35 ($30 members). Prize: $2,500+ in cash awards.

item.title: The Art of the Automobile · Sacramento Fine Arts Center
item.description: A juried show at the Sacramento Fine Arts Center in Carmichael, California, open to all art media with an automobile theme, with events around the exhibition sponsored by the United British Sports Car Club Sacramento. The judge is Kandi Thompson, a Sacramento-area watercolour painter of thirty-five years who has studied with nationally and internationally acclaimed artists, been a member of several art groups including the California Watercolor Association, and been published in Watercolor Magic and the Artists Magazine calendar. Photography is specifically accommodated: the rules exclude giclées and works made by any commercial printing process, but state the exception for photography. Work must be original, finished in the last three years, not previously shown in a juried show at Sac Arts, and available for sale, with a maximum size of 4 × 8 feet; hanging pieces must be wired with D-rings, and works over 29 × 35 inches must use plastic rather than glass. Up to three pieces per artist may be submitted at $25 each or three for $60, dropping to $20/$50 for members and $15/$40 for youth entrants. The centre retains a 50% commission on sales for non-members and 30% for members. Jury decisions are sent on 21 August, and the exhibition runs 8 September to 3 October 2026. — Deadline: August 12, 2026. Fee: $25 each or 3 for $60 ($20/$50 members, $15/$40 youth). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Annual Show of Small Works 2026 · Parklane Gallery
item.description: Parklane Gallery's Annual Winter Show of Small Works is a seasonal favourite in Kirkland, Washington, timed to the holiday shopping season so that visitors can buy work and take it home immediately rather than waiting for the show to close. Parklane is a co-operative gallery whose programme covers painting, photography, sculpture, glasswork and jewellery, and the call is open to any 2-D or 3-D artwork not previously shown at the gallery. Awards are $500 for first place, $300 for second and $250 for third, plus honourable mentions, additional special recognition awards, and separate miniature awards for pieces that meet the definition and quality of a miniature. The juror is to be announced. Hanging work must be no larger than 13 inches in height or width and 3-D work no more than 6 inches in any dimension; there is no lower size limit, and accepted pieces with an image area under 25 square inches may be shown in a separate Miniatures section. Entry is $25 plus $5 per piece for up to seven pieces per artist. The show is both hung and online: the juror chooses prizes from all accepted pieces, every accepted work goes into the online store when the show starts, and because wall space is limited some pieces hang in November and others in December. Notifications go out 28 September, accepted work is due 16 October, and the exhibition runs 4 November 2026 to 2 January 2027. — Deadline: September 23, 2026. Fee: $25 + $5 per piece (up to 7). Prize: $500 + $300 + $250.

item.title: Small Works, Big Joy 2026 · Arts Center East
item.description: A curated show at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut celebrating the power of small-format art and the craftsmanship, creativity and precision that flourish within limited dimensions. The exhibition hangs in the Eureka Gallery from 12 November to 19 December 2026 and stays open through the centre's popular Annual Holiday Artisan Fair. All media are welcome including painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, mixed media, printmaking, ceramics, fiber, metal and textiles, so long as the work meets the size limit: no piece may exceed 12 inches in any dimension, and sculptural works must fit within a 12-inch cube. Artists are encouraged to price work under $200. Arts Center East's standing rules for juried exhibits apply — open to artists 18 and over, up to five pieces each, no work shown in a previous ACE juried exhibit, all work original with no kits and no AI-generated art, and nothing made under instruction in a class, workshop or lesson. Entry is $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), rising by $5 per additional piece up to five. Wall-hung work must be wired with two loops and professional picture wire; sawtooth hangers and frames with triangular tabs are refused on arrival. The centre takes a 35% commission on sales for non-members and 25% for ACE artist members. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: $35–$55. Prize: Exhibition.
